independentDerivation.model: Fixed pivot; massless inextensible taut string; point-mass bob; fixed positive l and m; uniform gravity; negligible drag. Signed alpha is measured from the downward vertical; the positive tangent is the direction of increasing alpha.
independentDerivation.exactProjection: With r=(l sin(alpha),-l cos(alpha)) and unit tangent e_tau=(cos(alpha),sin(alpha)), gravity (0,-mg) projects to -mg sin(alpha). String tension is radial and has zero tangential projection. Hence m a_tau=-mg sin(alpha), a_tau=-g sin(alpha), and a_tau=l alpha''.
independentDerivation.linearization: For the entire swing satisfying |alpha| much less than 1 in radians, sin(alpha)=alpha+O(alpha^3). Thus a_tau approximately equals -g alpha. The retained equality sign in (1.8) is explicitly described as an approximation, not an exact finite-angle identity.
independentDerivation.arcCoordinate: Signed arc length s=l alpha is exact for radians and constant l. Therefore s''=a_tau, the exact equation is s''=-g sin(s/l), and the small-angle equation is s'' approximately equals -(g/l)s. Arc length is neither the chord nor horizontal displacement l sin(alpha).
independentDerivation.signsAndUnits: For ordinary libration around alpha=0, alpha and sin(alpha) have the same sign, so acceleration has the restoring sign. g/l has units s^-2 and (g/l)s has acceleration units. At alpha=0 the tangential acceleration is zero; radial acceleration v^2/l can remain nonzero.
independentDerivation.springComparison: The ideal Hookean spring obeys x''=-(k/m)x. Linearized pendulum and spring equations have the same form, not necessarily equal coefficients, periods, amplitudes or initial states. Their general linear solutions have two constants fixed by initial coordinate and velocity.
independentDerivation.timeDependence: For nontrivial oscillation the restoring acceleration changes with position and time. Constant-acceleration formulas are not valid over the whole oscillation.
